sources.publicationStatus: Final journal publication; metadata firstPublicationDate 2021-04-01. Version/access details below.

sources.design: Final2021 clinical practice guideline; distinct initial LAS and CAI evidence.
sources.population: Acute/postacute lateral sprains and chronic ankle instability, separately classified.
sources.comparator: Multiple rehabilitation/support comparisons, not one trial.
sources.coInterventions: External supports/manual therapy and education tailored to severity.
sources.outcomes: Acute: progressive weight bearing with external support, structured protected ROM/neuromuscular/balance rehab; severe injury may need up to10 daysimmobilisation. CAI: proprioceptive/neuromuscular exercise; supports alone insufficient for postural stability.
sources.uncertainty: Severity/healing/impairment assessment required; no self-prescribed acute fracture or severe-sprain protocol.
sources.limitations: Severity/healing/impairment assessment required; no self-prescribed acute fracture or severe-sprain protocol. Research candidate only; no clinical release.

protocol.execution: Acute protected active ROM, stretching, neuromuscular/postural/balance training; CAI proprioceptive/neuromuscular work.
protocol.dose: not reported as one universal set/repetition dose.
protocol.frequency: not reported as one universal frequency.
protocol.supervision: Clinic and home selected for severity, impairments, preferences and resources.
protocol.progression: Progressive weight bearing/protection and exercise selected for phase of healing; no universal increment.
protocol.stoppingRules: Severity, pain and protection guide care; no universal numerical stop rule.

sources.title: Effect of early supervised physiotherapy on recovery from acute ankle sprain: randomised controlled trial.
sources.publicationStatus: Final journal publication; metadata firstPublicationDate 2016-11-16. Version/access details below.

integrity.method: Publisher/PubMed records inspected during research; Europe PMC REST core metadata DOI:10.1136/bmj.i5650 rechecked during serialization, including publication type and comment/correction links. Not a registry-wide clearance.
integrity.result: Linked notices: Comment in: BMJ. 2016 Nov 16;355:i5984. doi: 10.1136/bmj.i5984; Comment in: J Physiother. 2017 Apr;63(2):115. doi: 10.1016/j.jphys.2017.02.006; Comment in: J Physiother. 2017 Apr;63(2):115. doi: 10.1016/j.jphys.2017.02.007 No claim of exhaustive integrity clearance or automatic supersession.

sources.population: Age≥16 with simple gradeI/II sprain; injuries requiring immobilisation excluded.
sources.comparator: Usual care versus added supervised physiotherapy.
sources.coInterventions: Usual care included graduated weight bearing and home-management information.
sources.outcomes: Excellent3-month FAOS recovery43%versus37%; difference6%(95%CI−3 to15); no clinically important functional improvement through6 months.
sources.uncertainty: No proof exercise is harmful/unnecessary for all injuries; the particular added supervised program did not improve major outcome.
sources.harms: Reinjury7.5%physiotherapy versus8.4%usual care; separate comprehensive harms extraction not established.
sources.limitations: No proof exercise is harmful/unnecessary for all injuries; the particular added supervised program did not improve major outcome. Research candidate only; no clinical release.

protocol.execution: Four-stage recovery-based active ankle ROM, isometrics and elastic-band/bodyweight resistance home exercises.
protocol.dose: Initial assessment plus up to7 further30 minclinic visits; home exercise dose based on recovery rather than one fixed regimen.
protocol.frequency: Individual appointment/home frequency; not fixed universal daily sets.
protocol.progression: Four stages: symptoms, ROM/strength/weight bearing, exercise tolerance, full function/dynamic stability; criteria for progression/discharge.
protocol.stoppingRules: not reported as an app-wide numeric stopping rule.
